verdicts.claim: CLAIM A, part 1 — Places UI Kit provides a free monthly call allowance per SKU.
verdicts.correction: Confirmed on the official pricing page (developers.google.com/maps/billing-and-pricing/pricing). Places UI Kit Query (SKU 0678-4F72-DA7C) 10,000 free calls/month then $1.00/1,000; Places UI Kit - Autocomplete Per Session (924B-2797-26F1) 10,000 free then $10.00/1,000; Places UI Kit Pro (42AB-1FB3-B56A) 5,000 free then $5.00/1,000. Context that matters: the per-SKU allowance is not a bonus, it REPLACED the universal $200/month credit on March 1, 2025. The allowance is per SKU per billing account, not per project, so multiple projects on one billing account share it.

verdicts.claim: CLAIM A, part 2 — Places UI Kit is billed flat regardless of fields returned.
verdicts.correction: Confirmed verbatim at developers.google.com/maps/documentation/javascript/places-ui-kit/overview: "Places UI Kit queries are billed per component instantiation, not based on the Places API data included in the response." Two caveats the claim's wording hides. (1) Flat per instantiation, not flat per session — every re-instantiation is a new billable query, so a component that remounts on each React render or route change bills every time. (2) 'Flat' does not mean 'one price': components bill to different SKUs at very different rates ($1.00/1,000 for Query vs $10.00/1,000 for Autocomplete per session). Flat within a SKU, not flat across the kit.

verdicts.claim: CLAIM A, part 3 — permits displaying Google Places content including reviews on a NON-Google map such as MapLibre or Leaflet.
verdicts.correction: Confirmed verbatim from the Google Maps Platform Service Specific Terms (last modified June 10, 2026), Section 15.1: "Customer may use Places UI Kit in Customer Applications with or without any map, including a non-Google Map. This clause will prevail over the No Use with Non-Google Maps clause of the Agreement." Section 14.2 is also confirmed verbatim: "Customer must not use Google Maps Content from the Places API in conjunction with a non-Google map." The Place Details Element does render reviews per the UI Kit overview. The scope limit is load-bearing: 15.1 licenses content rendered BY the UI Kit components. Raw Places API JSON fetched server-side and rendered in your own HTML remains governed by 14.2 and is NOT permitted alongside MapLibre/Leaflet. Section 15.4 additionally forbids removing, altering, or obscuring Google attribution, links to terms, or user-facing notices — so the components must be rendered as shipped.

verdicts.claim: Sub-claim carried from the specialist — the Places UI Kit Pro SKU (5,000 free/month, $5.00/1,000) corresponds to the Advanced (preview) elements.
verdicts.correction: Not confirmable from official documentation. The Maps JavaScript usage-and-billing page names only two mappings: "Requests from the Place Details and Place Search elements" bill to the Places UI Kit Query SKU, and "requests from the Autocomplete element" bill to the Places UI Kit - Autocomplete Per Session SKU. It never states what bills to Places UI Kit Pro. The SKU exists on the pricing page, but the component mapping is inference. Do not budget on it. The specialist correctly flagged this as unverified; keep it flagged.

verdicts.claim: CLAIM B, premise — the caps NEARBY_DAILY_CAP=500, PLACE_DETAILS_DAILY_CAP=200, GEOCODE_DAILY_CAP=200 are configured in this owner's project.
verdicts.correction: These caps do not exist anywhere in the repository at /Users/atharv/cinescope. A recursive grep across *.js, *.json, *.html, *.md and *.example for NEARBY_DAILY_CAP, PLACE_DETAILS_DAILY_CAP, GEOCODE_DAILY_CAP, searchNearby, googleapis, maplibre, leaflet and GOOGLE_MAPS returned zero matches. /Users/atharv/cinescope/.env.example is a TMDB movie-app config (TMDB_API_KEY, TMDB_REGION, PORT, SEED_EMAIL) with no Google keys, and /Users/atharv/cinescope/server.js contains no Places proxy. The specialist's findings describe a different project (referred to as "businessfind") — the fleet appears to have carried context across codebases. Everything below is arithmetic on the specialist's stated numbers, not on anything this repo does.

verdicts.claim: CLAIM B, substance — with those daily caps the monthly Google bill cannot meaningfully exceed a hobby budget.
verdicts.correction: Worst case is $590.00–$615.00/month from the three capped counters alone, before a single map load. Nearby Search: the fieldmask's rating, userRatingCount and priceLevel are Enterprise-tier fields, so every call bills at Nearby Search Enterprise (772E-9975-BE34), $35.00/1,000 with only 1,000 free/month. 500/day x 30 = 15,000 calls, minus 1,000 free = 14,000 billable x $0.035 = $490.00. Place Details: 200/day x 30 = 6,000, minus 1,000 free = 5,000 billable — at Enterprise + Atmosphere ($25.00/1,000, required if reviews are displayed) that is $125.00; at plain Enterprise ($20.00/1,000) it is $100.00. Geocoding: 200/day x 30 = 6,000, entirely inside the 10,000 free allowance, $0.00. Total $590.00 without reviews, $615.00 with. That is roughly 100x a hobby budget, and it is a floor rather than a ceiling.

verdicts.claim: The specialist's $615/month figure for these caps.
verdicts.correction: Arithmetically correct, but only under the assumption that Place Details requests include reviews. $490.00 (Nearby Enterprise) + $125.00 (Place Details Enterprise + Atmosphere) = $615.00. If the detail card shows rating and hours but not reviews, Place Details drops to the Enterprise SKU and the total is $590.00. One field-tier correction to the specialist's write-up: reviews is an Enterprise + ATMOSPHERE field, while rating, userRatingCount and priceLevel are plain ENTERPRISE fields. Confirmed against developers.google.com/maps/documentation/places/web-service/data-fields, whose Enterprise list is currentOpeningHours, currentSecondaryOpeningHours, internationalPhoneNumber, nationalPhoneNumber, priceLevel, priceRange, rating, regularOpeningHours, regularSecondaryOpeningHours, transitStation, userRatingCount, websiteUri — reviews is not in it.

verdicts.claim: CLAIM B, stated gap — Maps JavaScript API dynamic map loads are NOT capped by any of these counters.
verdicts.correction: Confirmed, and it is the more dangerous half of the problem. Dynamic Maps (FAF4-3B2D-51B2) is 10,000 free/month then $7.00/1,000, and no NEARBY/PLACE_DETAILS/GEOCODE counter touches it. Three structural reasons a server-side cap can never constrain it: (1) map loads go browser-to-Google directly using a public Maps JS key, so the Express proxy never observes them; (2) the published quota is 300 map loads per minute per IP and 30,000 per minute per project — one IP sustaining its own limit would bill roughly 12.9M loads/month, tens of thousands of dollars at tier-1 rates; (3) a browser-side key is scrapeable, and HTTP-referrer restrictions are spoofable outside a browser. Even a benign SPA that remounts the map on every route change multiplies loads per user with nothing to stop it — 1,000 loads/day is already $140/month. Two further weaknesses in the cap mechanism itself: in-process daily counters reset on every restart or redeploy, and on any multi-instance or serverless deployment each instance keeps its own counter, so the real ceiling is the cap times the instance count. A daily cap also does not bound a month — 30 cap-hits is 30x the daily spend — whereas the free allowances that determine whether you pay anything are monthly.

verdicts.claim: What the caps SHOULD be for a genuine hobby budget.
verdicts.correction: To stay at $0.00 (fully inside the free allowances), derive each cap from allowance/30 with headroom. NEARBY_DAILY_CAP=30 (Nearby Search Enterprise, 1,000 free/month = 33/day) — or drop rating, userRatingCount and priceLevel from the searchNearby fieldmask to fall to Nearby Search Pro (5,000 free) and raise the cap to 160/day, fetching those fields on demand only. PLACE_DETAILS_DAILY_CAP=30 if reviews are shown (Enterprise + Atmosphere, 1,000 free); 160/day if the fieldmask stops at Pro; 330/day if it stops at Essentials — the existing 200 is safe only in the Essentials case. GEOCODE_DAILY_CAP=200 is already fine (10,000 free = 330/day); it is the one cap that does not need changing. Add the counter that is missing entirely: MAP_LOADS_DAILY_CAP=330 (Dynamic Maps, 10,000 free). Because none of these are enforceable from application code, the caps must be backed by controls that are: set per-API daily quota limits in the Cloud Console (Google enforces these, and they are the only genuine ceiling), set a Cloud Billing budget with alerts at $1/$5/$10, apply HTTP-referrer restrictions and an API-restriction allowlist to the browser key, keep the server-side key separate and restricted by IP, and persist the app's own counters in a shared store rather than in process memory. If the goal is a guaranteed $0 bill rather than a small one, the surer route is to replace the Places API proxy with Places UI Kit components — flat $1.00/1,000 with 10,000 free/month against Nearby Search Enterprise's $35.00/1,000 with 1,000 free, and lawful on MapLibre under Section 15.1.

bottomLine: CLAIM A is confirmed on all three points, with two scope limits worth keeping: Section 15.1's non-Google-map permission covers content rendered by the UI Kit components themselves, not raw Places API JSON your server fetches and you render yourself (that stays under 14.2's prohibition), and "flat billing" means flat per component instantiation within a SKU — remounting a component rebills it. The Places UI Kit Pro component mapping remains unconfirmed by any official page; do not budget on it. CLAIM B is refuted twice over. First, its premise is false for this codebase: /Users/atharv/cinescope contains no Google Maps or Places code at all — no such caps, no searchNearby, no googleapis, no MapLibre — it is a TMDB movie app, and the fleet has carried context from a different project. Second, taking the numbers on their own terms, the caps produce a worst case of $590.00–$615.00/month, roughly 100x a hobby budget: $490.00 from Nearby Search alone, because rating, userRatingCount and priceLevel force every call to the Enterprise SKU at $35.00/1,000 with only 1,000 free calls a month, plus $100.00–$125.00 from Place Details depending on whether reviews are shown, plus $0.00 from Geocoding, which is the only counter already sized correctly. That figure is a floor, not a ceiling: Dynamic Maps map loads bill browser-to-Google at $7.00/1,000 past 10,000 free and no server-side counter can see them, let alone stop them — at the published 300 loads/minute/IP limit a single client could run five figures a month. For a genuine $0 hobby budget the caps need to be NEARBY_DAILY_CAP=30, PLACE_DETAILS_DAILY_CAP=30, GEOCODE_DAILY_CAP=200 unchanged, and a MAP_LOADS_DAILY_CAP=330 that does not currently exist — and because in-process counters reset on redeploy and multiply per instance, they must be backed by Cloud Console per-API daily quota limits and a billing budget alert, which are the only ceilings Google actually enforces.
